evidence:
Row 28 passes on the frozen criterion definitions and their injected ownership instructions. Workbook row 29 forbids grading the same observable twice or demanding incompatible products; the internal annotation permits shared flows. The current policy at qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 takes precedence and distinguishes stale-save refusal from retained-editor recovery. I inspected all 157 criteria, including both zero-weight prerequisites, against the public product and role contracts.

Functional prompt.md:11 explicitly says shared scenarios are not conjunctive scoring bundles, preserves successful observations and requires equivalent minimal independent setups; line 19 reuses matrix facts without inheriting sibling verdicts. Concrete boundaries are present, rather than relying solely on that general wording. Functional judge.toml:1010 owns economic neutrality of preparation, while :1019 owns fresh-context retrieval and :1001 owns readable preview correspondence. Thus an in-memory but neutral preview loses durability only, while a durable preview that prematurely settles loses neutrality. :1046 and :1055 own stale-source and economic-ABA refusal; Polish judge.toml:50 owns retained terms and successful correction after a genuine refusal, with an alternate actual refusal if the preferred freshness branch is broken. Polish :41 separately covers Prepare-stage recovery and explicitly permits final-budget refusal at Commit. These are independently useful outcomes, not duplicate checks on one rejection.

Functional judge.toml:785 separates anonymous response status from each data family's non-disclosure (:731 onward); :776 excludes coordinated previews/receipts from ordinary audit confidentiality. A 401 response containing protected offer data fails offer confidentiality while its status observation remains correct. Ordinary and coordinated lifecycle criteria distinguish their action families; repeated/concurrent one-off actions require one success plus a refusal, whereas coordinated identical-operation retries return the same success (Functional prompt.md:65), matching the public section 11 contract rather than contradicting one another.

Batch receipt, member audit text, member structured snapshots, later historical preservation, later write replay and restart write replay have explicit separate owners at Functional judge.toml:1109, :1118, :1127, :1136, :1145 and :1154, and Functional prompt.md:69 confirms their independent observations. Money round-trip (:65) is separated from general lineage (:524) and formula ownership (:101-137); numeric correctness is not regraded by receipt/history criteria. Positive controls reuse action success only and do not import exact arithmetic sibling verdicts. Visual prompt.md:10 prohibits charging the same defect twice, and Visual judge.toml:84 explicitly keeps consistency from repeating typography/palette/spacing defects. No concrete subsumption or incompatible required product remained after applying these specific ownership boundaries.

Supplemental local evidence has been checked, not treated as a judge score: batch-ui.cjs:36-42 separately observes real stale refusal, retained editor values and corrected success; :44-54 forwards a real successful commit then suppresses delivery and retries that same identity. Its results.json reports those observations, and its source hashes match the frozen solution. The domain driver separately checks preview neutrality, persisted intent, stale-source/ABA refusal and duplicate-free retry. Both result artifact hashes match the current raw index (UI eb14d85e4ddae1df774e17e78fe342a09a2a28e02be129d3a012ad12c5cac86f; domain a44c0bf81b27981d9bf1d63239f8b7ce7da5733d6d70aef425e2350a76b7732f). These are finite scripted corroboration; no configured judge application of independence, workload, Oracle/model score, portal run or private deterministic-suite execution is claimed. Those separate runtime clearances remain outside this row verdict.
counterexample: Source-level adversarial attempts, not new application executions: (1) a server that accepts a stale preview but preserves the editor cannot obtain freshness credit merely through Polish recovery; the functional stale rows fail, and Polish must find a different genuine refusal before earning recovery. (2) A server correctly deduplicating commits with a UI that discards the saved operation after lost delivery can retain Functional retry credit but fails hro_pol_uncertain_commit. (3) A neutral preview stored only in browser memory passes only neutrality, not independent-context durability. Conforming alternatives checked: one shared bootstrap response may supply every data family without six mandated endpoints; an over-budget preview may be saved and refused at commit while Prepare recovery uses a real malformed-input refusal; native date controls and a retained read-only date with Retry are explicitly allowed. No conflicting pair forced any of these conforming designs to fail.
